sources.relevant_excerpt: List of nationalities exempt from holding a visa: Albania, Andorra, Antigua and Barbuda, Argentina, Australia, Bahamas, Barbados, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Brazil, Brunei Darussalam, Canada, Chile, Colombia, Costa Rica, Dominica, El Salvador, Georgia, Grenada, Guatemala, Holy See, Honduras, Israel, Japan, Kiribati, Malaysia, Marshall Islands, Mauritius, Mexico, Micronesia, Moldova, Monaco, Montenegro, New Zealand, Nicaragua, North Macedonia, Palau, Panama, Paraguay, Peru, Samoa, San Marino, Serbia, Seychelles, Singapore, Solomon Islands, South Korea, St Kitts and Nevis, St Lucia, St Vincent and the Grenadines, Timor-Leste, Tonga, Trinidad and Tobago, Tuvalu, Ukraine, United Arab Emirates, United Kingdom, United States of America, Uruguay, Venezuela, Hong Kong Special Administrative Region, Macao Special Administrative Region, Taiwan, Kosovo. ... 'The exemption shall apply only to holders of biometric passports' (applies to Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, and Ukraine). ... 'The visa exemption applies to holders of passports of the Hong Kong Special Administrative Region.' ... 'The visa waiver applies to the holders of passports of the Administrative Region of Macao.' ... 'The exemption from the visa requirement shall only apply to holders of passports issued by Taiwan which include an identity card number.' China, India and Russia appear on the visa-required list.

sources.search_query: Portugal tourist visa fee (navigated from vistos.mne.gov.pt/en/)
sources.relevant_excerpt: General fee: '90 Euros'. Reduced fee: '45 Euros' (for children over 6 and under 12 years). Fee exemption for 'Children below the age of 6 (at the date of filing of visa application)'. Visa facilitation agreement countries (Albania, Armenia, Azerbaijan, Bosnia, Belarus, Georgia, Macedonia, Moldova, Montenegro, Serbia, Ukraine): '35€'. Cabo Verde: Adults 67.75€; Children 12-18 years 33.75€; Children under 12 exempt. 'The payment of the fee does not imply granting of the visa, nor does it entail refund in case of refusal.' External providers may charge up to half the visa fee (maximum 80€ normally, up to 120€ in exceptional circumstances where Portugal lacks consular representation).

sources.search_query: authorized Portugal visa application center (navigated from vistos.mne.gov.pt/en/)
sources.relevant_excerpt: 'According to your nationality and/or country of residency, if your country of residency is different from that of your nationality, refer to the Portuguese consular post below where to lodge a Schengen visa.' Channels: Portuguese Embassies and Consulates; External Service Providers (VFS Global, TLS Contact, BLS International, or others handling applications on behalf of Portugal); e-Visa Platform (https://pedidodevistos.mne.gov.pt/VistosOnline/?lang=ENG). Geographic tables (Africa, Americas, Asia/Oceania, Europe, Maghreb, Middle East) list designated submission points per country of residence; entries marked '(1) in representation of Portugal' are handled by another EU country's embassy. Examples: Brazil - Embassy in Brasilia plus VFS, or consulates in Rio de Janeiro and Sao Paulo; China - Embassy/Consulate in Beijing, Shanghai, Guangzhou plus VFS centers in multiple cities; United Kingdom - Consulates in London and Manchester plus VFS, or VFS in Edinburgh.

policies.policy_name: List of nationalities exempt from holding a visa (short stay / Schengen)
policies.description: Portugal's MFA visa portal publishes the list of nationalities exempt from the short-stay (Schengen) visa requirement, including special provisions for Hong Kong SAR and Macao SAR passports, Taiwan passports containing an identity card number, and biometric-passport-only exemptions for certain Western Balkan and Eastern Partnership countries.
conditions: Biometric passport required for Albania, Bosnia and Herzegovina, Georgia, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia and Ukraine
Taiwan passports must include an identity card number
Hong Kong and Macao exemptions apply to SAR passports

policies.policy_name: Schengen short-stay visa (tourism) via the Portuguese consular network
policies.description: Nationalities not on the exemption list must obtain a Schengen short-stay visa (up to 90 days in each 180-day period; tourism among the covered purposes; single or multiple entry) before travel. Applications are lodged at the Portuguese embassy/consulate designated for the applicant's country of residence, via external service providers (VFS Global, TLS Contact, BLS International) where designated, or online through the MFA E-Visa platform; in some countries another EU member state's embassy processes applications in representation of Portugal.
conditions: Travel medical insurance covering the entire stay required
Proof of means of subsistence (e.g. last three bank statements), return travel reservation, and accommodation proof (hotel reservation or statement of responsibility) required

policies.policy_name: Schengen area membership / EU free movement
policies.description: Portugal is a Schengen area member. Nationals of the other Schengen/EU member states listed on the official MFA page (including Germany and France) are not subject to Portugal's short-stay visa regime.
conditions: Derived from the official MFA Schengen-area membership list; the page does not itself elaborate free-movement rules
